name: Arevon Energy
headquarters: Scottsdale, Arizona, United States (regional office: New York)
ownership: private — 100% pension/sovereign capital at formation: APG (Dutch pension), CalSTRS, and a wholly owned ADIA subsidiary (~$1B buyout of Capital Dynamics' US Clean Energy Infrastructure platform, closed early 2022; current ADIA status unconfirmed — investor names dropped from recent boilerplate)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Arevon is the most Tesla-locked large buyer in the US — every one of its seven identified battery projects (~5.6 GWh including construction) runs on Megapack: Saticoy (142 units), California Flats (84), Condor (200 MW/800 MWh, plus a Tesla O&M contract), Vikings (the 'first US utility-scale solar peaker'), Eland 1&2 (172 Megapack 2 XL), Peregrine (200 MW/400 MWh), Nighthawk (300 MW/1,200 MWh, operational Aug 12, 2026), and Avocet (200 MW/800 MWh, planned). It is CAISO-centric (6.3+ GW owned/operated across 18 states, but every BESS is Californian), pension-owned, a transferability pioneer (the $191M JPMorgan Vikings deal was among the first IRA transfer transactions), and explicitly domestic-content-first — CEO Justin Johnson (permanent from Mar 2026 after Kevin Smith's abrupt February resignation) publicly frames the EV slowdown as 'saving our asses' by freeing US cell capacity, and predicts domestic cell oversupply through 2028. One tasking premise corrected: Big Rock (200 MW/400 MWh, LS Energy Solutions) is Gore Street's project, developed by Avantus — NOT Arevon's. The only visibly open OEM slot is Cormorant (250 MW/1,000 MWh, construction Mar 2026, COD 2027 — supplier unnamed as of the construction announcement), sitting squarely in the FEOC-constrained vintage.
ecosystemRole: We assess Arevon as the case study in single-integrator lock-in at scale: a ~1-2 GWh/yr CAISO buying cadence channeled entirely through Tesla, financed by a transferability machine (JPMorgan, Stifel, Wells Fargo, Blackstone/Goldman/Acadia preferred) whose ITC dependence makes FEOC compliance economically existential. For the relationship web it shows where the California RA market's storage dollars actually go — SCE, PG&E, San Diego Community Power, MCE, SCPPA offtakes flowing through Tenaska-originated projects into Lathrop-built Megapacks — and why a §154-named Chinese OEM faces a structurally hostile screen: pension owners, domestic-content marketing ('homegrown energy'), a safety-sensitized permitting environment (the Aug 2025 California Flats Megapack fire; Carson and Daly City municipal processes), and no ERCOT footprint where merchant economics might otherwise open a price door.

productsAndServices.name: CAISO standalone BESS fleet
productsAndServices.description: Saticoy (100 MW/400 MWh, Oxnard, COD Jun 2021, SCE 20-yr; co-owned with S&B USA); Condor (200 MW/800 MWh, Grand Terrace, COD Jul/Aug 2024, SCE 15-yr, Tesla O&M); Peregrine (200 MW/400 MWh, Barrio Logan San Diego, COD Jun 2025, ~$300M, SCE RA); Nighthawk (300 MW/1,200 MWh, Poway, COD Aug 12, 2026, PG&E long-term offtake); Avocet (200 MW/800 MWh, Carson, San Diego Community Power 15-yr ESSA, >$350M, COD target Q2 2026 — status unconfirmed); Cormorant (250 MW/1,000 MWh, Daly City, construction Mar 2026, $600M, MCE offtake, COD 2027 — the one project whose OEM is unnamed).
productsAndServices.positioning: The fastest per-GWh CAISO storage execution in the IPP tier — five operating utility-scale California BESS by mid-2025, all Tesla, mostly Tenaska-originated (Condor, Peregrine, Nighthawk; Avocet aligned).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term RA/ESSA contracts with SCE, PG&E, San Diego Community Power, MCE — the California community-choice and IOU offtake stack.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: CAISO resource adequacy and peak capacity.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 7-9 GW development pipeline (figures inconsistent across company statements); CDO Shanelle Montana signals growth via pipeline expansion 'and M&A activities.'

productsAndServices.name: Solar + storage hybrids
productsAndServices.description: Vikings (157 MWdc solar + 150 MW/600 MWh DC-coupled, Holtville, COD Nov 2024 — 'first US utility-scale solar peaker'; San Diego Community Power offtake; $529M; all major components US-manufactured: Tesla Lathrop, First Solar, Nextracker); Eland 1&2 (758 MWdc + 300 MW/1,200 MWh total, Mojave/Kern Co., full ops Aug 2025, ~$2B, SCPPA PPA serving LADWP + Glendale — ~7% of LA's load); California Flats BESS retrofit (~60 MW/240 MWh at the 280 MW solar site, 84 Megapacks).
productsAndServices.positioning: The Vikings 'solar peaker' framing — DC-coupled storage turning solar into dispatchable evening capacity — is the product California's post-NEM grid buys.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs (SCPPA/LADWP, SDCP); First Solar 2 GW US-made module supply agreement (Oct 2022).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Midwest solar expansion (Kelso 430 MW MO — Meta offtake, COD Mar 2026; Indiana fleet; Big Muddy IL) carries no announced storage yet.

productsAndServices.name: Financing & transferability machine
productsAndServices.description: A top-tier ITC-transfer innovator: Vikings $529M (Nov 2023) included a $191M ITC+PTC transfer to J.P. Morgan — among the first IRA transferability deals in the US (IJGlobal Renewables Deal of the Year); Condor $350M used Blackstone Credit preferred equity replacing traditional tax equity plus a Stifel ITC-transfer purchase; Nighthawk $920M (Mar 2026) = $482M debt + $169M Goldman Sachs Alternatives preferred + $268M tax-credit transfer to an unnamed corporate. $5.1B+ project financings in the trailing two years; $2.3B raised in 2025; $600M corporate revolver (expandable to $850M, Jul 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: Pension-capital cost advantage + serial preferred-equity/transfer structures — the financing sophistication benchmark for the IPP tier.
productsAndServices.roadmap: ITC dependence (~30-40% of capital stacks) makes FEOC-compliant supply non-negotiable for post-2025 vintages.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Arevon as effectively closed to a §154-named Chinese OEM on current settings: seven-for-seven Tesla concentration with O&M ties, an explicit domestic-supply doctrine from the CEO, pension-fund ownership screens, ITC-transfer dependence that makes FEOC compliance existential, and a predicted domestic cell oversupply through 2028 that removes the price-urgency argument for ~55%-tariffed Chinese imports.

(High confidence) We assess the Big Rock premise correction as strategically meaningful beyond hygiene: Arevon has NO LS Energy Solutions relationship — its integrator monogamy with Tesla is even purer than assumed, meaning there is no incumbent 'second vendor' precedent to point at when pitching a third.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Cormorant (1 GWh, OEM unnamed at construction start) as the only visible near-term opening — but with Primoris already EPC-mobilized, a 2027 COD inside FEOC-governed vintages, and Tesla as the house default, the realistic probability of a non-incumbent win is low; its value is as a probe of whether Arevon will ever dual-source.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the leadership transition (Smith's abrupt February 2026 exit, Johnson permanent in March, CFO seat interim) as a watch item rather than an opening: Johnson authored the domestic-supply thesis, and the safety-sensitized environment post-California Flats raises, not lowers, the bar for new vendors.

(Moderate confidence) For the Hithium lens: Arevon matters mainly as a market signal — it proves the CAISO RA offtake stack (SCE/PG&E/CCAs) will fund ~1-2 GWh/yr of storage through a single US integrator, and its no-ERCOT footprint means Hithium's likeliest merchant-Texas demand pool never intersects this account. Best long-shot contacts if ever pursued: David Peterson (VP Procurement), Jeremy Rand (SVP Project Execution, ex-SVP Procurement), Tommy Greer (CCO).
